title: Figma's Config lands in Bengaluru, and design starts writing things down
dek: Specs for design languages, why design still wins, accessibility for the agent era, and two fresh identities.
hero_alt: A wine sun over teal and green hills
summary: Figma brought Config to Bengaluru this week, and the headline is a shift toward writing things down: [a new Specs editor](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/14/figma-announces-new-features-to-define-how-agents-work-on-its-platform/) lets teams document their design language in Markdown so people and AI agents work from the same rules, while code layers move into public beta. On stage, Dylan Field [argued that design is still how products win](https://t2online.in/tech/tech-news/-design-is-how-you-win----figma-ceo-dylan-field-on-why-ai-can-t-replace-designers/2008651), naming India as Figma's second-largest market by daily use. That agent-heavy future raises the bar on inclusion too, with Deque making the case that [accessibility has to be a foundation](https://www.deque.com/blog/for-your-business-to-thrive-in-the-agentic-ai-era-treat-accessibility-as-foundational-to-your-ai-strategy/) of any AI strategy rather than an afterthought. On the brand side, [Pohoda Festival turns 30](https://www.itsnicethat.com/articles/andrej-and-andrej-pohoda-festival-30th-anniversary-graphic-design-project-141026) with a playful refresh and a futuristic typeface, and [Kuda gets an identity](https://www.itsnicethat.com/articles/barkas-kuda-graphic-design-project-131026) paced to Lagos.
